jurisdiction.name: Thailand
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Thailand governs AI through soft law and sector rules: the National AI Action Plan 2022-2027, guidelines from the Electronic Transactions Development Agency (ETDA) on generative AI and AI governance, AI risk-management guidelines from the Bank of Thailand and the insurance regulator, and national adoptions of the ISO/IEC 42001, 23894 and 42005 AI standards. The 2019 Personal Data Protection Act governs data used in AI. ETDA's consolidated Draft Artificial Intelligence Act, which replaced earlier drafts from 2023 and 2025, went to public hearing in July-August 2026 and awaits Cabinet approval.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Digital Economy and Society
Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation
narrative.review_notes: This review was first completed on 12 October 2026 and redone in a longer pass on 13 October 2026, covering the central law portal, Parliament, the government, each ministry and each sector regulator. Not yet verified from the official text: Royal Gazette search results and AI guidance from the securities, data protection and cybersecurity regulators, tracked as leads together with a Supreme Court AI instruction and a higher-education AI notification.

instruments.english_title: Thailand National AI Strategy and Action Plan (2022-2027)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation and Ministry of Digital Economy and Society (approved by the Cabinet)
instruments.current_status: Adopted plan covering 2022-2027. The title page states the version approved by the Cabinet on 26 July 2565 (2022). A 'Key Milestones and Progress' deck listed on the ai.in.th plan page reports an action plan revision for 2026-2027 after the National AI Committee meeting of 1 May 2025; a follow-on plan for 2028-2032 has been reported but no official document was found (see leads). An English summary of the plan is also published on ai.in.th.
instruments.summary: Six-year national AI action plan approved by the Cabinet on 26 July 2022, with the vision of a complete, integrated AI ecosystem that raises the economy and quality of life by 2027. It sets five strategies: preparing society, ethics, law and regulation for AI (ELSI); national AI infrastructure; AI workforce development (at least 30,000 AI personnel); AI technology and innovation; and promoting AI adoption in the public and private sectors, including sandbox mechanisms for AI start-ups. It assigns implementation to a national AI committee and lead agencies under the two proposing ministries.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; anchors ETDA's AI governance work, the AI ethics agenda and the draft AI law.

instruments.english_title: Bank of Thailand Policy Guideline on Artificial Intelligence Risk Management
instruments.issuing_authority: Bank of Thailand (IT Risk Supervision and Examination Department)
instruments.current_status: Issued 12 September 2025 (date on the cover). A draft with the English subtitle 'Guiding Principles for Artificial Intelligence Risk Management' was published by the BOT for public hearing in 2025 (https://www.bot.or.th/content/dam/bot/documents/th/laws-and-rules/hearing/120668%20AI%20Guideline%20public%20hearing.pdf); the final text adds an FAQ annex stating the guideline sets principles that providers apply according to their use.
instruments.summary: Bank of Thailand policy guideline for financial institutions, specialised financial institutions and regulated payment system and payment service operators on managing the risks of AI systems, whether developed in-house or obtained from third parties. It defines AI systems, identifies data, model-development and cyber-threat risks (including prompt injection, model inversion and data poisoning) and sets principles and practices in two parts: governance (board and senior management roles, customer disclosure and human oversight) and development and security controls across the AI lifecycle. It supplements BOT rules on IT risk, third-party risk, data governance and market conduct, and reminds providers that personal data and intellectual property laws still apply.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Sector regulator's AI risk-management expectations for banks and payment providers.

instruments.issuing_authority: Electronic Transactions Development Agency (AI Governance Center) with the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society
instruments.current_status: Announced by MDES and ETDA on 30 October 2024 (ETDA news page dated 30 ต.ค. 67, which links the e-book page carrying this PDF). The e-book currently served is a later revision of the launch text; no revision date is printed in the document. Voluntary guidance.
instruments.summary: Guideline for executives and staff of public and private organisations on governing the use of generative AI. Its five chapters explain generative AI, its benefits and limitations, its risks and how to manage them, models for deploying it in an organisation, and key considerations for governed use, with an appendix containing a sample organisational generative AI use policy. It extends ETDA's AI Governance Guideline for Executives and is voluntary.

instruments.summary: ETDA's first AI governance guideline for organisational leaders, presented as an English-language deck. It sets out a governance framework of three components (AI governance structure, AI strategy including responsible-AI strategy and AI risk management, and AI operation across the lifecycle), restates Thailand's six AI ethics principles, and maps practice to standards such as ISO/IEC 23894 and the NIST AI RMF. It is voluntary guidance for executives of public and private organisations.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Baseline national AI governance guideline later extended by the generative AI guideline.

instruments.summary: Government study by ETDA and NSTDA measuring the readiness of Thai public and private organisations to adopt AI for digital services, carried out to support the National AI Action Plan 2022-2027. It reports survey results on AI adoption, defines an AI readiness measurement and proposes future programmes and an AI governance framework for adoption. It is the 2023 baseline for later annual readiness surveys.

instruments.issuing_authority: King of Thailand on the advice and consent of the National Legislative Assembly acting as Parliament
instruments.current_status: In force. Section 2 brings the Act into force the day after publication in the Royal Gazette (28 May 2019), except chapters 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 and sections 95-96, which were to apply one year after publication; that later date was postponed by royal decrees (the text of the 2021 decree in Royal Gazette vol. 138 part 32 Kor has not yet been verified from an official source). The PDPC put a draft replacement Personal Data Protection Act to public consultation on law.go.th from 7 to 21 November 2025; its explanatory note contains no AI or automated decision-making provisions (see leads).
instruments.summary: Thailand's general data protection law, published in the Royal Gazette (vol. 136, part 69 Kor, p. 52) on 27 May 2019. It governs collection, use and disclosure of personal data, including for training and operating AI systems, sets lawful bases, data-subject rights, sensitive-data rules and cross-border transfer conditions, and establishes the Personal Data Protection Committee and its office. It has no AI-specific provisions.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law that applies to AI training and use.

instruments.official_title: ร่างพระราชบัญญัติว่าด้วยปัญญาประดิษฐ์ พ.ศ. ....
instruments.issuing_authority: Electronic Transactions Development Agency, Ministry of Digital Economy and Society (draft for public hearing)
instruments.current_status: Draft bill put to public hearing by ETDA on the Central Law System (law.go.th) from 9 July to 14 August 2026; the hearing has closed and no hearing summary or Cabinet approval was found. Not yet submitted to Parliament. It consolidates ETDA's earlier draft principles (2025) and draft AI promotion bill (2023). Draft section 2: in force the day after Royal Gazette publication, with chapters 3-5 applying 180 days later.
instruments.summary: ETDA's consolidated draft Artificial Intelligence Act, put to public hearing in July-August 2026, combining AI promotion and risk-based regulation. It provides AI testing (sandbox) projects, data sharing, standards and certification of support services; prohibits AI uses that manipulate users through subliminal techniques or cause wide-scale unfair discrimination; lets royal decrees designate high-risk AI (for health, environment, energy, telecoms, transport and similar areas) with duties for providers and deployers, plus transparency duties for deepfakes and chatbots. It gives the supervising office powers to order corrections and suspend services in serious incidents, and sets civil liability and administrative fines of up to 5 million baht.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Thailand's main draft horizontal AI law.
instruments.publisher_name: Office of the Council of State (Central Law System, law.go.th)
instruments.evidence_reference: law.go.th survey 7580 read via its API (curl); attached draft bill PDF read in full with pdftotext (615 lines, 7 chapters, sections 1-63+).

instruments.english_title: Draft Principles of the Law on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Electronic Transactions Development Agency, Ministry of Digital Economy and Society
instruments.current_status: Put to public hearing on law.go.th from 10 May to 24 June 2025 (dates stated in the hearing conclusion on law.go.th); 93 respondents, mostly supportive. A hearing summary was posted on 22 April 2026. Followed by the full Draft Artificial Intelligence Act put to hearing on 9 July 2026, which supersedes these principles.
instruments.summary: ETDA's draft principles for Thailand's first AI law, published for public hearing in May-June 2025. They propose a risk-based framework under which prohibited-risk and high-risk AI are not listed in the law itself but defined jointly by the enforcing agency and sector regulators, with duties falling on AI providers, deployers, importers and distributors. The consultation record states the principles create no licensing system, no new committee and no criminal penalties.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Policy blueprint for the 2026 draft AI Act.
instruments.publisher_name: Office of the Council of State (Central Law System, law.go.th)
instruments.evidence_reference: law.go.th survey 5316 record read via its API with curl (problem statement, principles, affected parties, necessity checklist and hearing conclusion).

instruments.summary: ETDA's 2023 draft AI promotion bill, designed to build an AI ecosystem with as few restrictive measures as possible. It provides seven tools: registration of AI, an AI innovation testing centre (sandbox), data sharing, standards, risk assessment, standard contract terms, and a fund to compensate damage from AI use, with the Minister of Digital Economy and Society in charge and a five-yearly review of the Act.

instruments.english_title: Guideline on the Governance of Artificial Intelligence Use for Insurance Companies (AI Governance Guideline)
instruments.issuing_authority: Office of Insurance Commission (Information Technology Group)
instruments.current_status: Published November 2025 (month and year printed on the cover; no day stated). It supplements OIC notices and guidelines already in force, such as IT risk management and outsourcing rules.
instruments.summary: OIC guideline for insurance companies on managing the new risks of using AI, applied proportionately to risk with emphasis on customer-facing and high-risk uses such as underwriting, premium setting and claims handling. It has four parts: AI governance (board oversight, an AI policy within enterprise risk management, three lines of defence and at least annual reporting on AI risk), robustness and AI security, transparency and explainability, and fairness and consumer protection. It also covers third-party AI services, human oversight levels and generative AI hallucination risks.

instruments.english_title: TCAS 42001-2567 Information technology - Artificial intelligence - Management system (national adoption of ISO/IEC 42001)
instruments.issuing_authority: Thai Industrial Standards Institute, Ministry of Industry
instruments.current_status: Published in the Royal Gazette on 17 July 2024 according to TISI's official standards catalogue. Voluntary standard. TISI has also issued มตช. 42006-2568 (requirements for bodies certifying AI management systems; no gazette date shown).
instruments.summary: Thai national certification standard (มตช.) adopting ISO/IEC 42001, setting requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an AI management system within an organisation. It applies to any organisation, whatever its size or type, that provides or uses AI-based products or services, and is the basis for certifying AI management systems in Thailand. Use is voluntary.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Thailand's national legislation and gazette, Parliament, the government, each ministry and sector regulators (including the central bank and the insurance, securities, data protection, cybersecurity and standards bodies) were searched. No qualifying document was found for procurement, cybersecurity or international agreements. Several official sites, including the gazette search and the securities, data protection and cybersecurity regulators, were unavailable, so documents reported there are listed as leads to check later.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: thin pass 2026-10-13 (second, longer deep review: up to 45 minutes, one agent, national level only, PROTOCOL §6; every existing record re-checked; each ministry and sector regulator searched one by one). Thin pass 2026-10-13: 6 existing records re-checked; dates previously taken from file names removed or re-sourced to issuer pages (PROTOCOL §4). law.go.th read via its own API (apig.law.go.th survey endpoints); draft PDFs on an AWS host used by law.go.th, so source_url = hearing page. Added Draft AI Act 2026, draft principles 2025 (promoted from lead) and 2023 draft bill (both superseded), OIC AI Governance Guideline (Nov 2025), TISI adoptions of ISO/IEC 42001, 23894, 42005 (primary_source_located: sold standards, metadata from TISI catalogue API). Not reached: ratchakitcha search 403, sec.or.th 403, pdpc.or.th 403, ncsa.or.th app shell, ai-ethics.onde.go.th and dgti.dga.or.th reset/503, opsc.coj.go.th reset, Thai FDA SaMD JS app, pr.moph.go.th 403. Draft AI Act english_title is a working translation. Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: Royal Gazette: PDPA 2019 re-read; gazette search portal returns 403 so AI terms were searched through web search restricted to ratchakitcha.soc.go.th (no AI-specific act, decree or AI provisions in other laws found; a 2021 MDES digital-ID notice mentions AI only in passing). Central Law System law.go.th searched through its own API: Draft AI Act (July 2026), draft AI law principles (2025), 2023 draft AI promotion bill and its two draft ETDA notices, NHSO AI chest X-ray payment drafts, and the draft replacement PDPA (no AI provisions). Krisdika: searched via law.go.th (run by the Council of State); no AI law. Courts: Supreme Court President's AI instruction (2025) located in news only (lead).; Parliament: parliament.go.th section 77 hearing list and search checked: no AI bill or deepfake bill listed; a 2023 motion for a special committee on AI was seen; People's Party draft AI bill reported in July 2026 but not found on parliament sites (lead).; Government: National AI Action Plan 2022-2027 (ai.in.th) re-read; ai.in.th page lists no revised plan document; MDES/ETDA AIGC guidelines re-read; MDES AI Ethics Guideline found on etda.or.th but undated (lead); ETDA 2022 recommendation paper and 'AI in Government Services' explainer (no date) not recorded; DGA AI Government Framework still unreachable (reset/503); no national AI committee founding instrument found in the gazette search; no AI procurement rule from the Comptroller General's Department found.; Ministries: Education (OBEC 2025 AI handbook cited in research only; no official copy found); Higher education (MHESI 2025 notification on AI teaching in curricula, news only, lead); Health (MOPH AI committee news only, no instrument; NHSO AI chest X-ray payment drafts, lead); Justice (no ministry AI document found; judiciary instruction is a lead); Defence (none found); Finance/tax (Revenue Department 2025 data governance notice, not AI-specific; no AI guidance); Labour (none found); Interior/police (none found); Agriculture (none found); Foreign affairs (none found); Consumer Protection Board (internal AI guideline 2026, lead).; Regulators: Bank of Thailand (2025 AI risk guideline re-read); SEC (two AI governance PDFs and an AI/ML handbook located, all 403, lead); OIC insurance (Nov 2025 AI Governance Guideline read and recorded); NBTC telecoms/media (no AI instrument found); Thai FDA medical devices (SaMD guidance page is a JavaScript app; no AI-specific document read); higher-education standards committee (see MHESI lead); Trade Competition Commission (no AI or algorithm guidance found); PDPC (draft AI guidance reported Feb 2026, pdpc.or.th 403, lead); NCSA cyber (AI Security Guidelines Oct 2025, no official copy, lead); TISI standards (ISO/IEC 42001, 23894 and 42005 adoptions recorded from TISI's catalogue; about a dozen more AI standards listed, lead).. Not reached: ratchakitcha.soc.go.th search and old DATA/PDF paths (403 to curl); searched only through web search; sec.or.th AI documents (403 to curl and WebFetch); pdpc.or.th (403); ncsa.or.th (JavaScript app; curl returns only the shell); ai-ethics.onde.go.th and onde.go.th (connection reset / 503); dgti.dga.or.th (connection reset / 503); opsc.coj.go.th (connection reset); coj.go.th search results load dynamically; medical.fda.moph.go.th SaMD page (JavaScript app); pr.moph.go.th (403 to WebFetch). Could not verify: NCSA AI Security Guidelines (1 Oct 2025) - no official copy; Supreme Court President's instruction on AI in court work (2025); MHESI notification on AI teaching in higher education (2025); SEC AI governance documents (403); PDPC draft AI guidance (Feb 2026); Royal decree postponing PDPA obligations (2021) - gazette link blocked. procurement, cyber-security, international: no material found.
Wording note 2026-10-19 (narrative.review_notes): The Royal Gazette's search and the securities, data protection and cybersecurity regulators' websites could not be accessed, so their AI guidance is tracked as leads, together with a Supreme Court AI instruction and a higher-education AI notification.
